result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.simrank_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Compute SimRank similarity between nodes. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.simrank_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Compute SimRank similarity between nodes. title: >- [Graph.simrank_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Compute SimRank similarity between nodes. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute SimRank similarity between nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L29250-L29379){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.simrank_similarity( source=None, target=None, importance_factor=0.9, max_iter=1000, tol=0.0001, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![SimRank similarity](../assets/graphs/simrank-similarity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Students ann, bob, and cy in a column on the left, courses math, art, and bio on the right. ann and bob, outlined in the accent color, take the same two courses, math and art (accent), while cy only takes bio. ann and bob are never linked directly, yet SimRank with C = 0.9 rates them 0.818 because their neighbors are alike; ann and cy share nothing and score 0.0." width="100%"} SimRank (Jeh and Widom, 2002) captures the idea that "two nodes are similar if their neighbors are similar". Every node is fully similar to itself (score 1), and the similarity of two different nodes is the average similarity of their neighbors (their in-neighbors on a directed graph), discounted by `importance_factor`. It is used for recommendation ("users who are linked to similar items"), finding related pages or papers in citation and link graphs, and matching roles across a network. A known quirk of SimRank is that nodes at an odd distance in a bipartite-like structure can score 0 even when they look related; `simrank_star_similarity()` fixes that by counting paths of every length. This method follows NetworkX's `simrank_similarity`, with the same defaults and results. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node (ID or label). If given alone, return its similarity to every node. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node (ID or label). With `source=`, return a single score. [importance_factor]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.9]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The decay `C` applied at each step, between 0 and 1 (default 0.9). [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations (default 1000). [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.0001]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance (default `1e-4`), applied as in `numpy.allclose`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to weight neighbors by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float, dict[int, float], or dict[int, dict[int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A single score when `source=` and `target=` are both given, the scores of `source` against every node when only `source=` is given, and otherwise the full table, keyed by node ID. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist, or the iteration does not converge. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} With the column-normalized adjacency matrix $W$ (columns summing to one over each node's in-neighbors), the scores are iterated as $S \leftarrow C \, W^\top S W$ with the diagonal reset to 1, starting from the identity, until successive iterates agree within `tol`. Each iteration costs two dense $n \times n$ matrix products, $O(n^3)$, so the method is meant for graphs of up to a few thousand nodes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two students who take the same courses are similar, even though they are not linked to each other: ::: {#afda22cd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["ann", "bob", "cy", "math", "art", "bio"]) g.add_edges( [("ann", "math"), ("ann", "art"), ("bob", "math"), ("bob", "art"), ("cy", "bio")] ) round(g.simrank_similarity("ann", "bob"), 3), g.simrank_similarity("ann", "cy") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.818, 0.0) ``` ::: ::: With only `source=`, the scores against every node come back as a dictionary: ::: {#127977ee .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} scores = g.simrank_similarity("math") {g.get_label_from_id(n): round(s, 3) for n, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'ann': 0.0, 'bob': 0.0, 'cy': 0.0, 'math': 1.0, 'art': 0.818, 'bio': 0.0} ``` ::: :::
